hints: Focus on the two reactions in sequence, oxidation followed by X + Y to make Z. What type of reaction joins an alcohol and its oxidation product?
Use the Mr values to work backwards. If Z is an ester, then Mr(Y) + Mr(X) - 18 = 172, so calculate Mr(Y).
Compare that Mr(Y) with what you get from oxidising primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols, and pick the alcohol class that fits.
walkthrough:
**Identify what X must be**

All four options have formula $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}\text{O}$. Check: $5(12) + 12(1) + 16 = 88$. So X is a pentanol isomer.

$$M_r(\text{X}) = 88$$

**Use the ester link to find Mr of Y**

Y reacts with alcohol X to make Z. This is classic esterification of a carboxylic acid with an alcohol:
$$\text{carboxylic acid + alcohol} \rightarrow \text{ester + water}$$
So masses follow:
$$M_r(\text{Z}) = M_r(\text{Y}) + M_r(\text{X}) - M_r(\text{H}_2\text{O})$$
$$172 = M_r(\text{Y}) + 88 - 18$$
$$M_r(\text{Y}) = 102$$

**Link Mr(Y) to oxidation type**

Heating under reflux with excess acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ is strong oxidation. A primary alcohol gives a carboxylic acid:
$$\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}\text{O} \rightarrow \text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_2$$
Check its Mr: $5(12) + 10(1) + 2(16) = 102$. This matches perfectly.

A secondary alcohol would give only a ketone ($M_r = 86$) which cannot form an ester. A tertiary alcohol would show no reaction.

**Pick the primary alcohol**

Only one option is a primary alcohol with the $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ group. That oxidises to $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCOOH}$ and then esterifies with itself to give $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCOOCH}_2\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_3$ of $M_r = 172$.

options.A: This is pentan-3-ol, a secondary alcohol. It oxidises to the ketone pentan-3-one ($M_r = 86$), not a carboxylic acid, so it cannot react with X to form an ester of $M_r = 172$.
options.B: This is 2-methylbutan-2-ol, a tertiary alcohol. It is resistant to oxidation by acidified dichromate(VI), so no compound Y would form at all.
options.C: This is 3-methylbutan-2-ol, a secondary alcohol. Like option A, it stops at the ketone stage and cannot undergo esterification to give Z.
options.D: This is 2,2-dimethylpropan-1-ol, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCH}_2\text{OH}$, a primary alcohol. Strong oxidation gives 2,2-dimethylpropanoic acid, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCOOH}$ with $M_r = 102$. Esterification: 102 + 88 - 18 = 172, exactly the $M_r$ of Z.
